dropped_findings.text: T-11 says appointment_event records who made each change. In the MVP every actor is the fixed 'staff', so events cannot tell staff members apart. The repudiation threat is still open, not covered by an existing control.

T-8 is about doctor fields leaking into appointment lists, but its mitigation cites C7, which is about patient medical history. C7 does not reduce this threat. The relevant control is that SUMMARY_SELECT stays unchanged.

T-5 (API and web type drift) and T-12 (shared-rule regression) are correctness risks with no attacker, labelled as STRIDE tampering. This makes the threat list look broader than its real security content.

cites.quote: T-2, T-3, T-4, T-6, T-7, T-8, T-9, T-11, T-13, T-14: covered by existing, cited controls.
AUTH-2: in the MVP every actor holds every permission.

findings.text: The Known section lists T-3 as covered by existing controls. T-3's own mitigation admits requirePermission grants every permission in the MVP, so it is a known gap, not an effective control.
